frontier.hypothesis: The residual is now stated at the allocator's input level: allocno 74 is INELIGIBLE for $v1 (hard-reg conflict) and carries no hard-reg preference, and both facts are fixed by the single-C-object model. Every route to changing either one lands on a second C object aliasing D_80106A73, which is the standing banned construct.
frontier.mechanism: A local-alloc-seated pseudo occupying $v1 across q's live range creates the conflict (local-alloc precedes global-alloc); global.c:1709-1713 records a preference only for a copy operand, and 74 is set from a bare symbol_ref, never copied.
frontier.next_probe: Only after a ruling or class grant covering a second address object. Do not re-run structural, declaration-order, value-sharing or type-narrowing searches -- s31 measured them with dumps and seven of them emit base's exact stream.

frontier.hypothesis: The structural modality is exhausted on this chassis in the strong sense: the forms that stay at 49 insns are RTL-invisible, and the forms that reach RTL move away from the target.
frontier.mechanism: cse/combine eliminate every added value object before global allocation, so the modality's levers cannot reach the contested allocno at all; the four bodies that do change codegen (v3 12, v4 30, v10 33, v11 14) each lose more than the seat convention is worth.
frontier.next_probe: None on this axis. If a future session wants a structural datum it should target the LOCAL-ALLOC seat directly, and the only C construct that reaches it is a second object -- currently banned.

frontier.hypothesis: The ladder's second cycle needs ten more sessions before disposition; the modality-count condition is already satisfied.
